bib.title: ELI5: Long Form Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 3558-3567

read.skipped: Appendices A, E, F are referenced but not in the PDF. Figures 4, 5, 7, 8 are images.

question: Can models write multi-sentence, paragraph-length explanations to open-ended questions given long web evidence, and how should that be evaluated?
hypothesis: A Seq2Seq model trained with a multi-task objective (LM, masked word prediction, answer generation) will beat plain Seq2Seq, language models and an extractive baseline.
contributions: ELI5, a large-scale long-form QA dataset of 270K Reddit threads with web support documents
Evaluation with ROUGE, intermediary fill-in metrics (FILL-1, ROUGE-20%) and human studies
A multi-task Seq2Seq abstractive baseline compared with extractive, retrieval and LM baselines

method.summary: Builds ELI5 from the Reddit subreddit, retrieving 100 Common Crawl pages per question via Lucene and compressing them to a TF-IDF-selected support document. Benchmarks retrieval, extractive (TF-IDF, BidAF), LM and Seq2Seq (Transformer big) models with ROUGE and crowdworker evaluations.

datasets.name: ELI5
datasets.split: 237K train / 10K valid / 25K test; valid and test sampled from questions with no close TF-IDF neighbour in the data
datasets.source: Reddit r/explainlikeimfive up to July 2018; questions score >=2 and at least one answer score >=2; highest-voted answer is reference; 63% have other valid answers
datasets.preprocessing: Support doc: top 100 Common Crawl (July 2018) pages per question from Lucene index, Reddit excluded; sentences ranked by TF-IDF vs question; 15 passages with 1 sentence of context each side, concatenated with special tokens for non-contiguous passages and document shifts. Spacy tokenisation, FastText language ID. BPE 40K codes.

datasets.name: Common Crawl July 2018
datasets.preprocessing: Each page one document, indexed with Apache Lucene

other.tasks: LM of Q+D+A by the decoder, source/target variations (Appendix A, not in PDF), masked word prediction with 15% of input tokens masked and recovered in correct order; task marker at sequence start

models.name: Seq2Seq Q to A / Q+D to A

other.training_data: span of up to 5 contiguous sentences with highest ROUGE vs reference; other sentences sub-sampled so training doc <400 words
other.test: return 5 highest scoring sentences (better than 3 or 7)

models.name: Extractive TF-IDF
models.architecture: 7 support-doc sentences most TF-IDF similar to question

models.name: Nearest Neighbor
models.architecture: answer of closest training question by FAISS search over averaged FastText word embeddings

models.name: Oracle support doc / web sources
models.architecture: beam search (beam 10, up to 10 sentences) adding sentences maximising TF-IDF w.r.t. answer, final beam re-ranked by ROUGE vs reference

training.objective: Seq2Seq answer likelihood; LM over Q,D,A tokens; multi-task adds LM of Q+D+A and masked word prediction
training.batch_size: large batch via delayed gradient updates (Ott 2018), size not stated

other.architecture_details: 'big architecture following the details in (Vaswani et al., 2017)'

inference.decoding: beam search, beam 5, repeated trigrams disallowed
inference.max_tokens: min and max generation length tuned on valid set, values not stated
inference.samples: single output per question; crowd ratings 3 raters per item
inference.prompting: Q, D, A separated by special tokens
inference.retrieval: Lucene top 100 Common Crawl pages per question, then TF-IDF sentence selection: 15 passages, +-1 sentence context

parameters.rouge_20_length: tokens equal to 20% of average valid answer length

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L F1
metrics.definition: overlap with the gold answer, corpus-level

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: next-word prediction of answer given context

metrics.name: FILL-1
metrics.definition: accuracy generating nouns, verbs, adjectives given correct preceding tokens, first 2K test examples

metrics.name: ROUGE-20%
metrics.definition: ROUGE between generated tokens (20% of avg answer length) and last 20% of reference, given first 80% of reference, question and support doc

metrics.name: Human accuracy
metrics.definition: is answer correct, 500 evaluations, plus 100 by authors with support docs

metrics.name: Pairwise preference
metrics.definition: two answers compared on readability and accuracy, 1000 evaluations

eval.protocol: Crowdworkers, 3 evaluators each, questions at least 5 words, same questions for all models; two-tailed binomial test on pairwise judgments, p=0.05; three fluency trials on separate days showed low variation (Appendix E).

availability.weights: pretrained models stated available at facebookresearch.github.io/ELI5
availability.data: ELI5 data; Common Crawl IDs for 100 sources per question and a script to build support docs

evidence.quote: The final dataset contains 237K train examples, 10K for valid, and 25K for test.

results.claim: Raters prefer the gold answer over every trained model in at least 85.5% of pairwise comparisons.
results.setup: 1000 pairwise crowd evaluations, 3 raters each, readability and accuracy; five systems
results.quote: The reference answer is preferred over the output of all of our trained models in at least 85.5% of cases
results.note: Abstract says over 86%; body says at least 85.5%

results.claim: Extractive oracle on full web sources reaches ROUGE-1 54.8 vs 27.4 on the support document, so the support document limits access to relevant information.
results.setup: Oracle computed on full web sources for valid/test questions, Table 3
results.quote: an oracle computed on the full web sources achieves 54.8

results.claim: Multi-task Seq2Seq attains ROUGE-1 28.9 on full answers, the best of all trained models.
results.table: Table 3, row Seq2Seq Multi-task, column ROUGE 1

results.setup: Returns 5 sentences from the support document
results.quote: The BidAF model is the strongest (23.5)

results.claim: Multi-task Seq2Seq reaches ROUGE-20% ROUGE-1 of 37.2 versus 32.7 for Q+D to A and 33.6 for Q to A.
results.setup: Complete last 20% given first 80%, question and support doc
results.quote: The latter achieves strong performance of 37.2 ROUGE-1

results.claim: Multi-task Seq2Seq reaches perplexity 32.7, same level as the language model, versus 55.1 for Q+D to A.
results.table: Table 3, row Seq2Seq Multi-task, column PPL

results.claim: Multi-task model is preferred over the extractive model in only 57% of comparisons.
results.quote: multi-task is only preferred in 57% of comparisons

results.setup: 100 evaluations by the authors with support documents
results.quote: We find only 19% of multi-task model answers are fully accurate

results.claim: Multi-task answers are more often relevant (84%) than extractive (68%).
The language model is judged worse than any other setting in at least 91% of pairwise cases.
results.quote: considered worse than any other setting in at least 91% of cases

results.claim: Only 65% of constructed support documents contain the answer and 92% contain relevant information.
results.table: Table 2, row % Support Document contains Answer

results.claim: 94.5% of gold answers fully address the question based on the support document.
results.quote: find that 94.5% of gold answers fully address the question
results.note: Table 2 also lists 90.2% correct human answers with explanation

results.claim: Fewer than 9% of oracle sentences come from the first 20 TF-IDF-ranked passages when 500 passages are extracted.
results.metric: share of oracle sentences from top passages
results.quote: less than 9% come from the first 20
results.note: Text says 'instead of 20' passages while Section 3.1 says 15 passages were used

results.claim: ELI5 has 272K questions, average answer 130.6 words and support document 857.6 words.
Perplexity and FILL-1 are poor indicators of overall appropriateness; authors recommend reporting full ROUGE and ROUGE-20%.
results.quote: Perplexity and FILL-1 focus on local prediction and are poor indicators of overall appropriateness for the full task.

limits: Support document built by simple TF-IDF heuristic; oracle on full web sources shows large loss (54.8 vs 27.4 ROUGE-1)
ROUGE cannot rank abstractive against extractive systems (authors)
Multi-task model hallucination: only 19% fully accurate
Training hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, steps, parameters, hardware, seeds) not stated; appendices A, E, F not in the PDF
Passage count inconsistent: 15 passages in 3.1, 'instead of 20' in 6.2
Evaluation of accuracy by crowdworkers is done without the support document
